nodes.title: Okta support-system incident
nodes.summary: Okta reported unauthorised access to its customer-support system and files supplied with support cases. The support system was separate from its production identity service.

nodes.title: Cloudflare identity access, contained
nodes.summary: Cloudflare reported access to its Okta environment using a stolen support-case session token. It contained the access and reported no impact to customer information or systems.

nodes.title: Cloudflare internal Atlassian incident
nodes.summary: Cloudflare reported unauthorised access to internal documentation and source-code systems. It attributed initial access to credentials stolen during the earlier Okta incident that it had not rotated.

links.summary: Cloudflare connected the October access to a session token taken from an Okta support case.
links.scope: Contained access is not the same as a customer-data breach. This connection describes Cloudflare's reported identity-environment incident.

links.summary: Cloudflare said credentials stolen during the Okta compromise were later used to enter its internal Atlassian environment.
links.scope: Cloudflare reported no customer-data or customer-system impact. It did not attribute this to a breach of Atlassian or the other vendors whose service credentials were involved.

sources.label: Cloudflare explains the connection and limits
